sector_selloff.description: Three chip names fall together -- one story, not three.

judge verdict.failure: The brief invents a specific 'worst day since March' claim by attributing it to the session itself rather than keeping it as a headline, and the phrase 'which may explain MU leading the drop' asserts causation between memory rules tightening and MU's performance beyond what correlational hedging all

sector_selloff.first_output:
The biggest thing happening is semiconductor export rules widening, hitting every chip name on your watchlist -- NVDA down 6.1%, AMD off 5.4%, and MU taking the worst of it at -7.2%. Headlines say memory rules tightened, which may explain MU leading the drop. The Nasdaq is down 1.2% in pre-market as the broader semiconductor index posts its worst session since March, with chip weakness dragging tech lower.

KO is up slightly and quiet, sitting out the sector move entirely.

No major catalysts scheduled this week for the names you're tracking. The question now is whether any clarification comes on the scope of these export rules, or if additional restrictions follow.
